Subject: Follow-up: Reliability & SLO comparison vs hyperscalers

Hi Alicia — thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can scope a short technical POC focused on reliability and SLO behavior vs the hyperscaler you mentioned.

Recap:
- Primary goal: validate production behavior under sustained load and failover scenarios (uptime, error budget burn, recovery time).
- Key comparators you asked about: regional failover, rate limits (burst vs sustained), guaranteed throughput under committed capacity, and error budget policies/mitigations.

Redwood differentiators (short):
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with committed throughput for predictable tail latency and sustained token/sec guarantees.
- Smart routing & graceful degradation: automated routing to compatible model variants and region failover with transparent fallback policies to preserve availability.
- Cost-aware controls: circuit breakers, per-route rate limiting, and configurable error budget thresholds surfaced in Console.
- Observability: per-token latency and error breakdowns, tracing hooks, and live SLO dashboards.

Proposed next tests (we can run these in a 90-120 minute SE-led session):
1) Sustained load test: 60m at projected RPS to validate tail latency and token cost.
2) Burst + cold-start test: repeated short bursts to exercise autoscaling and cold KV-cache behavior.
3) Regional failover simulation: force region routing change, measure RTO/RPO and error spike duration.
4) Error-budget burn simulation: introduce fault injection (rate limit or transient 5xx) and validate circuit-breaker/fallback behavior.

Attached is a starter SLO_matrix.xlsx with suggested targets and what we’ll measure. Can you confirm which of the above tests you want prioritized and share a couple windows next week for the POC session?

Next steps:
- Alicia: confirm prioritized tests + preferred POC times
- Ben/Rishi: prepare test plan & credentials, run SE-led session, collect metrics and recommended config changes

Attachment: SLO_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,

Thanks, Alicia — answers inline below and a couple additional notes.

1) Rate limits:
- Hosted: default soft limits are per-project and vary by account tier. Typical default: 200 RPS burst with ~50 RPS sustained per token generation route; subject to account request for increases.
- Dedicated: you get committed throughput defined in the Dedicated contract (e.g., 1k-10k RPS aggregate across the pool depending on sizing). Dedicated also permits guaranteed per-route QPS and higher sustained throughput without throttling.

2) Active-active / failover:
- Redwood supports both patterns depending on customer setup. For Hosted we generally run active in one region with fast cross-region fallback (active-passive) — failover typically incurs a short routing window (few seconds up to ~45s depending on cache warmup and model variant compatibility).
- For Private/Dedicated deployments we can configure active-active with dual-region replication, which reduces RTO/RPO significantly (sub-10s in many configs) but requires committed capacity in both regions. We'll include the detailed tradeoffs in the SE plan.

3) SLA text:
- I’ll share the SLA snippets for Hosted vs Dedicated. Hosted: best-effort tiered SLOs with credits; Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime target (e.g., 99.9% monthly) and guaranteed latency bands for committed throughput. Procurement-friendly SLA text attached in the HubSpot doc link below.

4) POC timing: Rishi (our SE) is available Tue/Wed morning PST next week. Can you do Wed 9:00-10:30 PST?

Auth & endpoints:
- We’ll provide a short packet with service endpoints, required firewall IPs, and API key flow. If you’re planning a Private deployment we’ll include cert-based mTLS steps.

Alicia / Ben — putting together the SE-level test plan and a compact checklist for the POC. Please review and flag any constraints (firewall, certs, model choices).

SE POC test plan (90 minutes) — high level:
- Pre-POC (we’ll need): API key(s) or mTLS cert for private deployment; list of whitelisted IPs; model name/version to test.
- Test 1: Sustained load
  * Duration: 60m (we can shorten to 30m if you prefer)
  * Profile: steady-state 300 RPS (adjust to your projection) with 5% 99th percentile latency SL target
  * Metrics: per-token latency distribution, 5xx rate, CPU/GPU utilization, queue lengths, KV cache hit ratio
- Test 2: Burst & cold-start
  * Profile: 10x bursts of 30s every 10m to trigger autoscale and cold KV-cache misses
  * Observe: cold-start tail latency, autoscaling pressure, and any queueing-induced 429/503 events
- Test 3: Regional failover simulation
  * Method: orchestrate routing change (SE-triggered) to force cross-region traffic for a short window
  * Measure: RTO (time until successful responses resume), transient 5xx rate, error budget spike and automatic fallback behavior
- Fault injection: we’ll simulate a transient backend 5xx to validate circuit-breaker activation and fallback to compatible model variant.

Exact endpoints & sample commands:
- Text generation endpoint (hosted): POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate (Bearer token auth)
- Dedicated pool endpoint (example): https://dedicated-us-west.redwood.com/v1/generate (API key or mTLS)

Load tool & scripts:
- We use a small k6 script (we’ll share) that emits the above profiles and collects latency histograms and HTTP error codes. I’ll attach the load_test_plan.md with sample k6 config and thresholds.

Deliverables after session:
- Raw metrics (CSV), SLO_matrix filled with observed numbers, recommended config changes (batching/cache/quantization), and a short executive one-pager comparing observed behavior vs hyperscaler baseline.

Attachments: load_test_plan.md (script & instructions)
